A1.justification: Both 11-page PDFs describe the same RapVerse work and support comparison of text, equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix or embedded supplement. Pages 2–11 are identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original vocal and motion generation experiments in Table 2, ablations in Table 3, and a user study in Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original generation experiments, ablations and user-study results in Tables 2–3 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same compositional motion VQ-VAEs, Vocal2unit audio tokenizer, autoregressive generation model, token organization and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English rap coverage: Rap-Vocal contains 108.44 hours from 32 singers, and Rap-Motion contains 26.8 hours. The vocal and whole-body motion generation tasks are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains T2M-GPT, MLD, Habibie et al., Talkshow, EMAGE, MotionCraft and the cascaded system for motion comparisons, and FastSpeech2 and DiffSinger for vocals. Figure 4 also retains the same comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 retain the same metrics, 85%/7.5%/7.5% train/validation/test split, and user study involving 20 participants and ten 10-second test videos.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Table 3 retain the same ablations examining a pretrained language model and a single motion tokenizer. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report vocal MOS with 95% confidence intervals in Table 2(b). There are no changes to uncertainty reporting, run-count or seed information, or statistical testing.

E6.justification: All reported dataset statistics, benchmark scores, ablation results and user-study findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains the proposed model's motion FID of 17.58, BC of 0.485 and vocal MOS of 3.64 ± 0.15.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations 1–5 and the accompanying definitions and reasoning are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: the RapVerse dataset, unified generation from lyrics, modality tokenization, and performance competitive with specialized systems.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning temporal synchrony, error accumulation in cascaded systems, and facial-detail loss with a single VQ-VAE are unchanged. No substantive qualifications or limitations are added or removed.

D1.justification: Dataset processing, tokenizer and inference details, and project-page access information are unchanged. No implementation settings, hardware information or reproducibility disclosures are added.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research-positioning statements and all 71 reference entries are identical. No cited work or novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: v3 adds affiliation 5, MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab, to Chuang Gan alongside affiliation 1, UMass Amherst. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the scientific prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The second author line is slightly recentered to accommodate the added affiliation superscript, and the margin stamp is updated. Figures 1–4, Tables 1–3 and the remaining page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 adds institutional attribution and updates version information, with only a negligible title-page layout adjustment. The methods, empirical evidence, reasoning, clarity and reproducibility information remain unchanged, supporting no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
